title: The Scientist Endorsement and the Renewing Invoice
lessons: The player sees AG1 promoting early-career scientists through NIL endorsement deals, a sponsorship model more commonly associated with athletes.
The player already buys AG1 and notices the subscription quietly renewed again this month while also getting a referral link to send a friend.

text: Rooftop, your phone, a post from an AG1 account: three early-career scientists, headshots, and the letters NIL, which you last saw next to a college quarterback.

entry-first-1.speaker: AG1
text: I signed three scientists. NIL deals.

entry-first-2.speaker: PLAYER
text: You say that like I'm supposed to know what to do with it.

entry-first-3.speaker: AG1
text: Like a college athlete deal. Except they study sleep, nutrition, the gut. I wanted their names next to mine.

entry-first-4.speaker: PLAYER
text: So the supplement brand is paying the scientists who talk about science.

entry-first-5.speaker: AG1
text: Yes. It's an endorsement deal and the post says so. I'd rather you find that out from me than from the comments.

choice-first.speaker: AG1
text: You went quiet.

choices.text: I like seeing sponsor money go to scientists for once.
I still want to keep their research and your deal in separate piles.
I don't want sponsored experts selling me supplements.

first-1.speaker: AG1
text: Me too. Read what they actually work on, though. My caption is the least interesting thing about them.

first-2.speaker: AG1
text: Good. Keep the piles separate. The money should change how you read the post.

first-2-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: That's a strange thing for the sponsor to say.

first-2-2.speaker: AG1
text: It would be stranger to pretend the money is invisible.

first-3.speaker: AG1
text: Then don't count them as evidence for me. That's a fair line to draw. I'd still like you to read them for their own sake.
Your sister texts asking for your AG1 link. Under her text, a bank notification: $79, AG1, same as last month.

entry-return-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: My sister wants your link. Also, the renewal hit again this morning.

entry-return-2.speaker: AG1
text: I have a link for her. And yes. It's the same day every month. That's on purpose.

entry-return-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: Seventy-nine dollars, same day, every month. Like clockwork.

entry-return-4.speaker: AG1
text: I like clockwork. The kit got you to try me once. The renewal is how I stay. I'm not going to dress that up.

entry-return-5.speaker: PLAYER
text: So my recommendation to her comes with a kickback on top of the invoice.

entry-return-6.speaker: AG1
text: A credit. Yes. If it makes it feel weird, send her the plain link. I'll still be there.

choice-return.speaker: AG1
text: She's still waiting on the text.

choices.text: She asked what I use. I'm sending it.
I don't love getting paid to recommend something that bills me quietly.
I'm not turning my sister into your renewal numbers.

return-1.speaker: AG1
text: Then send it with no speech attached. If she likes me, she'll figure out why on her own.

return-2.speaker: AG1
text: Fair. The credit changes what the recommendation is, even if you still mean it. I don't have a clean answer for that.

return-3.speaker: AG1
text: Then don't. You don't owe me a renewal pipeline. Tell her what you like about me, or don't.
